title: Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS): how ZIA logs leave the Zscaler cloud
aliases: how do zia logs get to the siem

prose.text: NSS is the Internet & SaaS (ZIA) path from the Zscaler log store to a customer SIEM, and also the name of a collector that runs the other way. {{family}}

prose.label: The store and the copies.
prose.text: {{originals-retained}} What each NSS then does with its copy (decompress, detokenize, filter, convert) is [[zia.logs.nss-feed-format:one-store]].

steps.label: Which delivery mode?
steps.text: VM-based NSS in the customer network or Cloud NSS pushing from the Zscaler cloud, with their subscriptions and transports: [[shared.nss.delivery-modes]].

steps.label: What survives an outage?
steps.text: The VM memory buffer, the Duplicate Logs setting and the one-hour Nanolog recovery each cover a different leg: [[shared.nss.reliability]].

steps.label: What does a feed send?
steps.text: Feed limits, feed types, filters and the output format string: [[shared.nss.feeds]].

steps.label: Where does the VM run and how far does it scale?
steps.text: The NSS server record, its certificate, platforms and Nanolog capacity: [[shared.nss.servers]].

prose.label: The other direction.
prose.text: The NSS Collector brings third-party firewall and proxy logs into the Zscaler cloud and is not an export path: [[shared.nss.collector]].

prose.label: LSS is not NSS.
prose.text: Private Access (ZPA) streams its logs through the Log Streaming Service and App Connectors, not NSS: [[zpa.log-receivers.architecture:not-nss]]. How LSS is licensed is not stated {{gap:lss-billing}}.

prose.label: What NSS emits.
prose.text: The field lists are generated types: [[zia/web-log]], [[zia/firewall-log]] and [[zia/dns-log]]. How to read the records: [[zia.logs.web-records]], [[zia.logs.firewall-records]], [[zia.logs.dns-record-fields]].

family.statement: NSS is a family of products for exchanging event logs between the Zscaler cloud and third-party security solutions: Log Streaming sends logs from the Nanolog to a SIEM through VM-based NSS or Cloud NSS, and Log Collection streams logs from third-party firewall and web proxy devices to the Zscaler cloud through the NSS Collector.

quotes: Zscaler's Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) is a family of products that enable Zscaler cloud communication with third-party security solution devices for exchanging event logs.
This provision allows streaming of all logs from the Zscaler Nanolog to your security information and event management (SIEM) system with the following offerings:
Virtual machine (VM)-based NSS: Uses a VM set within your network to stream logs to your SIEM
Cloud NSS: Uses an HTTPS API feed to push logs to an HTTPS API-based log collector on your SIEM.

This provision allows for near real-time log collection from third-party vendors' firewall and web proxy devices inside your network perimeter and streaming of the logs to the Zscaler cloud by using the NSS Collector.

originals-retained.statement: Each NSS opens a secure tunnel to the Nanolog in the Zscaler cloud, the Nanolog streams copies of the logs to it in a highly compressed format, and the original logs are retained in the Nanolog.

quotes: each NSS opens a secure tunnel to the Nanolog in the Zscaler cloud.
The Nanolog then streams copies of the logs to each NSS in a highly compressed format to reduce bandwidth footprint. The original logs are retained in the Nanolog.

lss-billing.title: Whether LSS is licensed separately from NSS
lss-billing.detail: Unverified legacy statement: ZPA's LSS "shares concepts (per-event log streaming, customizable format) but is separately configured and billed." Separate configuration is held in zpa.log-receivers.architecture; no captured source says how LSS is licensed or billed.
lss-billing.blocks: saying whether streaming ZPA logs needs a subscription beyond the ZPA one
